sanskrit:
लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः।
छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः।।
caption:
Chapter 5, Verse 25

Kṛṣṇa lists the qualifications for Nirvāṇa. ‘labhante brahmā-nirvāṇam ṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇa-kalmaṣāḥ’ (Those who are free from anger and all material impurities, who are self-realized, self-disciplined, and constantly engaged in the welfare of all... attain liberation). ‘chinnadvaidha’ (Doubts cut off). ‘yatātmānaḥ’ (Self-controlled). ‘sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ’ (Busy working for the welfare of all). This refutes the idea that liberation is selfish. The true sage works hard to help others because he knows they are suffering in ignorance.
